== Biography ==

'''Barbara Glasgow''' is documented as the mother of [[Little-6307|Catharine Little]], born 9 September and baptised 29 September 1611 in Edinburgh parish, Midlothian. Her parents, actual birth date and birthplace, marriage and death have not been established. The baptism names [[Little-6308|Johne Little]] as Catharine's father; it establishes co-parenthood, but not a marriage between him and Barbara.

Barbara emerges in the historical record through her connection to the Little family in Edinburgh, the capital city of Scotland. In the early 17th century, Edinburgh was a significant administrative and religious center. Barbara's only confirmed vital event documented so far is the birth and baptism of her daughter in 1611, recorded in the Edinburgh Parish register (Midlothian). The details are:<ref name="Catharine1611">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4N-CDX : 16 September 2021), Johne Little in entry for Catharine Little, 1611. Citing Edinburgh Parish, Edinburgh, Midlothian, Scotland. Details also corroborated by FindMyPast transcription.</ref>

* '''Child''': [[Little-6307|Catharine Little]] (Born: 9 Sep 1611, Baptised: 29 Sep 1611)
* '''Father''': [[Little-6308|Johne Little (abt.1580-aft.1612)]]
* '''Mother''': '''Barbara Glasgow'''

No marriage record to Johne Little or death record has yet been definitively linked to Barbara.

== Research Notes ==

=== Birth estimate and church identification ===

Barbara has been estimated to have been born circa 1586, possibly in Scotland.<ref name="BirthEst">This birth year is estimated based on the 1611 birth of her daughter Catharine, assuming Barbara was in her early-to-mid-twenties at the time, a common age for mothers in this era. This is a genealogical estimation only and is not based on a birth record.</ref> This calculation assumes that she was about 25 in 1611. It does not establish her actual age or birthplace; Edinburgh is the location of her daughter's recorded birth and baptism.

The High Kirk (St Giles'), St Cuthbert's and Canongate Kirk have been suggested as possible baptismal churches. No cited record identifies the church, and the suggestion remains unverified.

=== Parentage and relationships ===

[[Glasgow-3522|William Glasgow]] and [[Herbison-439|Margaret Herbesoun]] are possible parents whose relationship to Barbara remains unproved. Glasgow town-clerk protocols 2903 and 2916 (1586) identify the couple as parents of [[Glasgow-1099|George Glasgow]]; neither names Barbara or calls her George's sister. George's description as son and heir does not mean that he was their only child, but it supplies no relationship to Barbara.<ref name="GlasgowProtocols1586">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 9, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc01scogoog/page/n113/mode/2up protocol 2903, printed p. 103, 15 July 1586], and [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc01scogoog/page/n116/mode/2up protocol 2916, printed p. 107, 1 September 1586].</ref>

No Barbara Glasgow/Johne Little marriage has been identified in the published Edinburgh marriage register for 1595–1700. Same-name John Little identities remain unresolved; the negative search does not prove that Catharine's parents never married. Johne is her proved co-parent, while marriage remains unproved.

The household or immediate collateral circle of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] is a possible family origin. Ninian's son Robert was a cordiner; his probable son William moved into Leith, and William's son entered a cordiner apprenticeship. The possible later Barbara records concern South Leith and an Edinburgh cordiner. These occupational and geographical correspondences supply a hypothesis, not proof that Barbara was Ninian's daughter or niece. The hypothesis also depends on resolving whether the adult Barbara records concern one woman.

=== Disambiguation: Contemporaries and Potential Conflation ===
Barbara Glasgow occurs in several early seventeenth-century Edinburgh and Leith records. The maternity, Wilson marriage and Johnstoun marriage may represent different adult women or successive events in one woman's life; continuity has not been proved. The following identities and records require comparison:

* '''Barbara Glasgow, wife of George Johnstoun:''' (Likely [[Glasgow-3302|Barbara (Glasgow) Johnson (abt.1600–)]]). [https://www.familysearch.org/tree/person/details/9VM1-52D FamilySearch profile 9VM1-52D] appears to '''conflate''' this woman's records with the mother of Catharine Little. Records associated with this Barbara include:
** Marriage to George Johnstoun on 21 November 1616 in Edinburgh Parish.<ref name="JohnstounMarriage1616">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYMH-HZJ : 11 February 2020), Barbara Glasgow in entry for George Johnstoun, 1616.</ref>
** Several children christened in Edinburgh Parish with George Johnstoun between 1617 and 1627, including Daniell (1617)<ref name="Daniell1617">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YQ-BX4 : 16 September 2021), Barbara Glasgow in entry for Daniell Johnestoun, 1617.</ref> and Archebald (1618).<ref name="Archebald1618">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1Y3-2XL : 16 September 2021), Barbara Glasgow in entry for Archebald Johnstoun, 1618.</ref> (Other children mentioned in the source list for FS profile 9VM1-52D include Marione, Margaret, James, and Catharine Johnstoun).
** The estimated birth year of c. 1596 associated with FS profile 9VM1-52D would make the Johnstoun bride about 20 in 1616, but the mother of Catharine about 15 in 1611. This age comparison has favoured distinguishing the records; both birth estimates are conjectural and cannot establish separate identities.

* '''[[Glasgow-3182|Barbara (Glasgow) Wilson (abt.1590–)]]:''' Married [[Wilson-126696|John Wilson (1590–)]] on 26 November 1611 in South Leith Parish, Midlothian (adjacent to Edinburgh).<ref name="WilsonMarriage1611"> "Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYML-ZBB : 11 February 2020), Barbara Glasgow in entry for John Wilson, 1611.</ref>

* '''[[Glasgow-1102|Barbara Glasgow (1617-)]]:''' Baptised 29 June 1617 in Edinburgh Parish, daughter of George Glasgow and Margaret Steuart. She cannot be the adult mother recorded in 1611.<ref name="Barbara1617">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-JYX : 12 February 2020), Barbara Glasgow, 1617.</ref>

Given these contemporaries, it is crucial that further research confirms any additional records genuinely belong to the Barbara Glasgow who was mother to Catharine Little in 1611.

=== Identification summary ===

* '''Defining Record:''' This profile represents the Barbara Glasgow named as mother to Catharine Little, born 9 Sep 1611 and baptised 29 Sep 1611, daughter of Johne Little.<ref name="Catharine1611"/>
* '''Conflation Alert:''' FamilySearch profile 9VM1-52D appears to conflate this Barbara with Barbara Glasgow, wife of George Johnstoun (married 1616). Records require careful separation.
* '''Multiple name-bearing records:''' The records have been interpreted as at least three, possibly four, Barbara Glasgows in the Edinburgh/Leith area between 1610 and 1620. The 1617 child is certainly distinct from the 1611 mother, but the number of distinct adult women remains unresolved.
* '''Conflicting Birth Estimates:''' Circa 1586 assumes maternal age about 25 in 1611; circa 1596 assumes bridal age about 20 in 1616. These explain the competing calculations, but neither is a recorded birth date.
* '''Parentage & Origin Unknown:''' No sources confirming Barbara's parents, specific origin, marriage, or death have been identified.
* '''Wilson date conflict:''' The indexed Wilson marriage above is dated 26 November 1611. Research also identifies a South Leith entry dated 20 September 1611 for Barbara Glascow and Johne Wilsoune. The relationship between those dates requires the original entries; neither establishes continuity with Catharine's mother.
